 Tired Of Sharing Berths? Indian Railways May Bring Big Changes To The RAC System
 Indian Railways is reviewing its existing Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) ticket system. The Railway Board is considering some changes to make train journeys more comfortable. 
 by Priyanshi Shah 
 Updated: November 13, 2026 1:17 PM 
 Share 
 Cover Image Courtesy: Wikimedia Commons 
 In train travel, it’s important to have a comfortable seat, especially during overnight journeys. One of the most uncomfortable arrangements is an RAC ticket, where two passengers have to share one berth. Now, Indian Railways is planning changes to its existing Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) system. Here’s what you can expect! 
 What Is Indian Railways Planning For RAC? 
 In an RAC ticket, two passengers have to share a single berth, but they both pay the full fare. So, Indian Railways is now reviewing the system to examine whether it needs any changes. According to a Times of India report, an official said that charging the full fare when passengers get only a shared berth may not be appropriate. 
 Apart from the fare structure, passenger comfort is another concern. Indian Railways is also exploring new arrangements to make journeys more comfortable. If a male and female passenger get the same berth, it can sometimes become uncomfortable, especially when they need to sleep. A parliamentary committee also suggested reviewing this system. 
 Also Read:  Indian Railways: Passenger Trains To Run Beneath Bullet Train Station For The First Time 
 Is Indian Railways Planning To End The RAC System? 
 There is no official confirmation on whether Indian Railways is planning to end the RAC system entirely. The Railway Board is still reviewing the system. Until then, passengers will have to wait for an official announcement and continue travelling under the existing RAC system. 
 What Is RAC? 
 With the RAC system, passengers can still travel even if their tickets are not confirmed. It works as a middle option between confirmed and waitlisted tickets. Personally, if you ask me about my experience travelling under the RAC system, it’s super uncomfortable. You can’t even stretch your legs properly.

 FAQs
 What is RAC ticket?
 An RAC ticket allows passengers to travel on a train even without a confirmed berth, but they may have to share one berth with another passenger.
 What is the difference between confirmed and RAC tickets?
 A confirmed ticket gives a passenger a full seat, while an RAC ticket allows them to travel but requires them to share a single berth with another passenger.
 Which is the longest train in India?
 The Dibrugarh–Kanyakumari Vivek Express is the longest train route in India.
